stem: During adolescent development, what is the pattern of decline in delta EEG power across the brain?

options.text: It declines first at occipital sites and last at frontal sites
It declines first at frontal sites and last at occipital sites
It declines uniformly across all cortical regions simultaneously
It only declines in the parietal and temporal lobes
It increases first at occipital sites and last at frontal sites

explanation: Delta EEG power declines in a posterior-to-anterior pattern during adolescent brain maturation, with occipital sites changing before frontal sites.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because delta EEG power follows a posterior-to-anterior decline, with occipital regions changing before frontal regions.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because this reverses the typical maturation pattern; frontal regions are usually the last to show the decline.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the decline is regionally patterned rather than occurring everywhere at once.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the decline is not restricted to only the parietal and temporal lobes.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the change is a decline in delta power, not an initial increase.

source.hint: The pattern matches the sequence of dendritic pruning in brain development.
